jurisdiction.venue: Court of First Instance, High Court of Hong Kong

headline: Fourteen Years After RMB 302 Million Cash Overstatement, Hong Kong Court Bars Three China Longevity Directors — With HK$0 in Fines
deck: Under a Carecraft agreed-facts order obtained by the S.F.C., former chairman Lin Shengxiong and executive director Zhang Hongwang drew 10-year board bans, Huang Wanneng received four years, and all three were ordered to pay legal costs only.

financials.amount_display: RMB 302.4M Overstated Cash (19.9% of Net Assets)
financials.fine_display: HK$0 Monetary Fine (SFC Legal Costs + 4–10 Yr Bans)

score_provenance.rationale: Fourteen years after China Longevity overstated cash by RMB 302.4 million (19.9% of net assets), three former executive directors resolved civil SFO section 214 proceedings via Carecraft agreed facts with HK$0 in monetary fines and zero prison time, mitigated only by 4-to-10-year Hong Kong board disqualifications and SFC legal costs.

street_crime_compare.exec_summary: Hong Kong’s Court of First Instance disqualified three former China Longevity Group executive directors for 4 to 10 years under SFO section 214 over RMB 302.4 million (~$42M) in overstated cash—with HK$0 in monetary fines and zero prison time fourteen years after auditors flagged the shortfall.
street_crime_compare.street_equivalent: Inflating a small business’s bank statement by 20% to reassure lenders, keeping the shares frozen for twelve years, and agreeing to sit out of corporate directorships while paying only court fees
street_crime_compare.street_sentence: Criminal false-accounting charges and custodial exposure in ordinary commercial fraud cases, versus civil board bans and legal costs here

sources.title: SFC obtains disqualification orders against three former directors of China Longevity Group Company Limited over material financial misstatements and disclosure failures
sources.agency: Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), Hong Kong

interactive_art_spec.caption: Hong Kong’s High Court Building on Queensway in Admiralty, where the Court of First Instance issued 10-year and four-year corporate disqualification orders against three former executive directors of China Longevity Group Company Limited.
